A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching analyses moved into v2's appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original representation-similarity measurements, probing experiments, cross-layer and cross-context evaluations, and arithmetic layer-removal results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical analyses and adds experiments with a new probe, activation steering, and ordinal-data decoding.

M1.justification: V2 introduces param-sin, assigning each latent feature a sine wave with learnable frequency, phase, and amplitude, beyond v1's inherited sinusoidal-basis probe (Section 3.2, Equation 2). It also adds target-conditioned activation steering using optimized patch embeddings and interpolation; v1's intervention removes layers.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds decoding of weekday names, month names, and written numerals from 'one' to 'ten', extending the evaluated task beyond digit-valued number representations. The original eight natural-language datasets across four domains and the BBC multi-token-number setting remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds lin, bin, and log comparators to the arithmetic output-decoding experiments, where v1 examined sinusoidal probing (v2 Figure 7 versus v1 Section 4.2). The prior sin probe also becomes the explicit comparator in the new steering and ordinal experiments. The earlier TunedLens comparison is retained.

E3.justification: The Figure 3a probe comparison changes from synthetic arithmetic contexts to natural-language contexts, and Figure 5b expands held-out-layer evaluation from three to six models. New protocols include leave-one-out ordinal validation and steering incorrect predictions with an interpolation factor optimized per layer, operation, and probe. Newly disclosed hyperparameters alone do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds a mechanistic intervention study comparing activation steering across layers and probe types (Figure 9), plus an error analysis reporting that temporal decoding failures persist at the first position when token order is reversed. V1's layer-removal, sparsity, and transformer-component analyses remain in Appendices A.6–A.8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a defined uncertainty-estimation procedure. The added leave-one-out evaluation changes validation design rather than introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds output-probe results, steering that corrects up to 30% of multiplication errors and 42% of division errors under optimized settings, and ordinal results including 11/12 month names decoded by param-sin across six models. Input, cross-layer, and conditional output-recovery plots also change alongside the new probe and settings. These are not straightforward same-setting gains over v1; Table 2's earlier results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 2 adds a mathematical definition of the parameterized sinusoidal probe and its single-sine-wave constraint. The revision does not add formal theorems or proofs; its principal new mechanistic support is experimental.

C1.justification: V2 adds an explicit new-probe contribution and extends the main claims to ordinal information and activation steering. Its introduction strengthens v1's error-tracing account into a claim that sinusoidality determines arithmetic accuracy, while the conclusion centers the necessity of specialized interpretability tools. The underlying universality claim is retained.

C2.justification: V2 interprets improved output decoding as challenging prior gradual-refinement accounts and develops stronger arguments about misleading general-purpose probes. New limitations address English-centric models, three-family coverage, exclusion of models above 30B parameters, and a suspected zero-index blind spot. Appendix A.8 also newly qualifies layer removal because correct lower-layer predictions are scarce.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents initialization, regularization, optimizers, learning rates, dimensions, training steps, checkpoint selection, and steering optimization, substantially expanding v1's sparse implementation account. These are largely new disclosures, not demonstrated changes to old settings. Conversely, v1's explicit description of uniform number replacement for balancing natural-language contexts is omitted.

R1.justification: V1 primarily extends Kadlcik et al.'s probe; v2 positions its own architecture against that probe's generalization limitations and explicitly challenges Zhou et al.'s gradual-refinement interpretation. It adds connections to Engels et al. on ordinal representations and Mickus et al. on embedding structure, while removing broader motivation references such as Kalai et al. This substantially revises the contribution's positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around universality and specialized probing tools. V2 adds an explicit contribution list, reframes Section 4, moves several mechanistic analyses into the appendices, and adds Limitations, Experimental Details, and an LLM-use disclosure. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main layout from one column to two, reorganizes existing figures, and moves several displays into the appendices. It adds output-comparison and steering figures, an ordinal-results table, and a non-number Fourier-spectrum display. Figures 3 and 5 gain new series, and Figure 4's caption clarifies the color and line-style meanings.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central probing evidence through explicit output-baseline comparisons, targeted interventions, and ordinal generalization tests. Appendix B addresses v1's sparse implementation documentation, while new limitations clarify applicability. These gains improve the paper's assessability and reproducibility. The stronger causal wording still needs qualification: steering uses known correct targets and optimized interpolation, so its reported benefits do not establish a generally deployable error-correction method.
